Young King is a 2024 American drama film written and directed by Bryant T. Griffin. Produced by Selena Leoni, the film stars Vincent Washington, Tarra Riggs, Kirby Griffin, Vaughn Wilkinson, and James Arthur Sims.
The narrative follows an Iraq War veteran struggling with undiagnosed PTSD as he attempts to reintegrate into civilian life in North Carolina, exploring themes of trauma, family dynamics, and the systemic lack of resources for returning soldiers.
The film premiered at the 2024 American Black Film Festival (ABFF), where it won the Jury Award for Best Actor (Vincent Washington). It was subsequently acquired for distribution by Buffalo 8.
Premise
Diondre Howell, a war veteran with undiagnosed PTSD, finds solace with Fatimah, a young woman in the process of rebuilding her life. Diondre's mother, Zoe, encourages him to find treatment, but he is repeatedly denied health care due to his discharge type from the military: "Other-than-honorable."
As Diondre struggles to cope with his shame and trauma, he must find help before his increasingly self-destructive behavior hurts the people he loves the most - his family.
Cast
* Vincent Washington as Diondre Howell
* Vaughn Wilkinson as Isaiah Howell
* Tarra Riggs as Zoe Howell
* James Arthur Sims as James Howell
* Kirby Griffin as Fatimah Danel
Release
Young King had its world premiere at the American Black Film Festival on June 15, 2024. It was also an official selection at the Austin Film Festival and the Pan African Film Festival.
In 2025, the film was acquired by Buffalo 8 for North American distribution. It was released on video on demand (VOD) platforms in November 2025.
Reception
Young King has received recognition on the film festival circuit for its realistic portrayal of PTSD and veteran life.
Awards and nominations:
* American Black Film Festival (2024): Won the Jury Award for Best Actor (Vincent Washington).
* Pan African Film Festival (2025): Won the Programmers' Award for Best Narrative Feature.
* Austin Film Festival (2024): Official Selection.
* '''Martha's Vineyard African American Film Festival (2024): nominated for Best Feature Film for the Best of the Best Award (presented by HBOMax)
* Sunscreen Film Festival' (2024): Won Best Narrative Feature, Best Actor, and Best Cinematography.
The film has been praised for its "authentic and real" presentation of trauma. Nerds That Geek gave the film a positive review, noting that it [https://nerdsthatgeek.com/film/austin-film-festival-movie-review-young-king "holds nothing back in showcasing the truth"] regarding the lack of support for veterans in America.
